👟✨ The Shrinking Shoes An original passage written for LearnAce 1 Leo bought a pair of red sneakers at a strange little shop with no sign. "Be careful," the shopkeeper warned. "They grow small when you tell a lie." 2 At dinner, Leo's mother asked if he had finished his homework. "Yes," he said — and his toes began to pinch. When his teacher asked who had broken the class pencil sharpener, Leo said, "Not me," and the shoes squeezed so tightly that he hopped in pain. 3 That night Leo told the truth about both. ⛸️❄️ Ice Skates on the Rideau An original passage written for LearnAce 1 In the winter of 1910, Marie laced up her father's old skates on the frozen Rideau Canal in Ottawa. Her skates were too big, so she stuffed her mother's knitted socks into the toes. 2 Back then, there were no snow-clearing machines on the canal. Families shovelled their own paths across the ice. Marie's brothers cleared a long, winding lane from their house to the market so the family could skate there to buy bread. 3 Today, the Rideau Canal Skateway is cleared by machines and is one of the longest skating rinks in the world. But on cold mornings, Marie's great-granddaughter still stuffs a pair of knitted socks into her skates — just for luck. Why did Marie's brothers clear a path to the market?

choices: So the family could skate there to buy bread

examples.question: 🐎✉️ The Last Run of the Pony Express An original passage written for LearnAce 1 In October 1861, sixteen-year-old Billy galloped across the Nevada desert with a leather pouch of letters strapped to his saddle. Riders like him changed horses every fifteen kilometres so the mail could cross the country in just ten days. 2 At the station, the keeper handed him a cup of water and some news. "Telegraph lines reached California today," he said. "Messages can cross the country in minutes now." 3 Billy looked at the thin wire stretched along the poles. He patted his tired horse. "Then let's make this last ride a good one," he said, and he raced off into the setting sun. What can you infer will happen to the Pony Express?

Bread Around the World An original passage written for LearnAce 1 Almost every culture in the world has its own kind of bread. In India, people cook flat, round chapati on a hot pan. In Mexico, tortillas made from corn have been eaten for thousands of years. In France, long, crusty baguettes are sold fresh every morning. 2 Some breads rise and some stay flat. Breads that rise, like baguettes, contain yeast, a tiny living thing that makes bubbles of gas in the dough. Flatbreads like chapati and tortillas usually contain no yeast at all. What makes some bread rise?

choices: In spring, when days are warm and nights are freezing

The Invention of Basketball An original passage written for LearnAce 1 In 1891, James Naismith, a Canadian teacher working in Massachusetts, needed an indoor game to keep his students active during the cold winter. Every time someone scored, a person had to climb a ladder to get the ball out of the basket! Years later, someone cut the bottoms out of the baskets. 3 Today basketball is played by millions of people in more than two hundred countries. Which detail shows that basketball is popular today?
